title: Writing the Incident Report 📄
description: Executive summaries, technical reports, and lessons learned documentation.

slides.title: The Final Deliverable 📦
slides.content:
# Turning Chaos into a Coherent Document

The **Incident Report** is the official record of what happened. It serves three audiences:

1.  **Executive Leadership:** What was the business impact? Is it over? What are we doing to prevent recurrence?
2.  **Technical Team:** What were the IOCs, timeline, and root cause? (For future reference).
3.  **Legal / Insurance:** Documentation required for claims and potential litigation.

**Three Report Types in One:**
- **Executive Summary** (1-2 pages)
- **Technical Findings** (Detailed Timeline, IOCs, MITRE ATT&CK Mapping)
- **Lessons Learned & Action Items**

slides.title: Executive Summary Structure 📈
slides.content:
# Speaking to the Board

Executives have limited time and need to make business decisions.

**Section 1: Incident Overview (1 paragraph)**
- **What happened?** (One sentence: 'On April 20, 2026, Acme Corp experienced a ransomware incident affecting the Accounting file server.')
- **How was it detected?** ('The incident was detected by our EDR platform at 08:32 UTC.')
- **Current Status:** ('Systems are fully restored. Enhanced monitoring remains in place.')

**Section 2: Business Impact**
- **Downtime:** ('The Accounting file server was unavailable for 6 hours.')
- **Data Exposure:** ('Forensic analysis indicates no evidence of customer data exfiltration.')
- **Financial Cost:** ('Estimated remediation costs: $75,000 in external consultant fees and overtime.')

**Section 3: Root Cause (High-Level)**
- ('The initial access vector was a phishing email that bypassed email filters.')

**Section 4: Remediation & Next Steps**
- ('Implemented Multi-Factor Authentication on all admin accounts.')
- ('Enhanced email security filtering rules deployed.')
- ('Full security awareness training scheduled for Q2.')

**Section 5: Lessons Learned**
- ('Communication delays occurred due to outdated contact list. Process updated.')

**Length:** **1-2 pages maximum.**

quizData.question: Which of the following details is MOST appropriate for the Executive Summary of an incident report?

options.text: The exact SHA256 hash of the ransomware executable.
The command line arguments used by the attacker's PowerShell script.
The estimated financial impact of the service outage.
A full packet capture analysis showing the C2 beaconing interval.

quizData.explanation: Executives care about business metrics (money, time, risk). Technical details belong in the Technical Findings section.

slides.title: Technical Findings Section 🔬
slides.content:
# The Forensic Record

This section is for **internal security teams, future investigators, and potentially expert witnesses**.

**Required Subsections:**

**1. Incident Timeline (UTC)**
- **Format:** `[YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS UTC] - Event Description - Source of Evidence`
- **Example:** `[2026-04-20 08:15:22] - Phishing email delivered to jsmith@acme.com - O365 Message Trace`
- **Importance:** This is the single source of truth for what happened when.

**2. Indicators of Compromise (IOCs)**
- **Network:** IPs, Domains, URLs, JA3/S SL fingerprints.
- **Host:** File Hashes (MD5, SHA256), File Paths, Registry Keys, Mutex Names, Scheduled Task Names.
- **Email:** Sender addresses, Subject lines, Attachment names/hashes.

**3. MITRE ATT&CK Mapping**
- Map each phase of the attack to a Technique ID.
- **Example:** Initial Access: T1566.001 (Spearphishing Attachment) -> Execution: T1059.001 (PowerShell) -> Persistence: T1053.005 (Scheduled Task).
- **Value:** Standardized language for describing adversary behavior.

**4. Forensic Evidence Summary**
- List of evidence collected: 'Memory dump of FS01 (fs01-20260420.raw)', 'Disk image of FS01 (fs01-C-Drive.E01)', 'Firewall logs (2026-04-20.csv)'.
- Hashing information to prove integrity.

**5. Detailed Analysis Narrative**
- A prose description of the attack chain, referencing the timeline and IOCs.
- This tells the **story** of the incident.

slides.title: Example: Technical Timeline Format ⏱️
slides.content:
Precision is non-negotiable. Use a consistent format.

**Bad Timeline:**
```
Morning: User clicked bad link.
Afternoon: We found malware.
```

**Good Timeline:**
```text
[2026-04-20 08:15:22 UTC] Email from invoice@paypa1.com with subject 'Invoice 456' delivered to bob.smith@acme.com. Attachment: Invoice_456.xlsm (SHA256: abc123...). Source: O365 Message Trace.
[2026-04-20 08:32:10 UTC] User bob.smith opened attachment and enabled macros. Source: Sysmon Event ID 1 on BOB-LAPTOP.
[2026-04-20 08:32:15 UTC] Process 'EXCEL.EXE' (PID 1234) spawned 'powershell.exe' (PID 5678) with command line '-Enc SQBFAFgA...'. Source: Sysmon Event ID 1.
[2026-04-20 08:32:45 UTC] Process 'powershell.exe' (PID 5678) initiated outbound connection to 185.142.53.179:443. Source: Sysmon Event ID 3.
[2026-04-20 08:33:00 UTC] SIEM Alert 'Suspicious PowerShell Network Connection' generated. Source: Splunk.
```

**Why is this better?** It's precise, includes evidence sources, and can be independently verified.

slides.title: Lessons Learned & Action Items ✅
slides.content:
# Turning Pain into Progress

This section is the bridge from **Post-Incident** back to **Preparation**.

**Structure:**
| Finding | Root Cause | Action Item | Owner | Due Date | Status |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Email filter missed phishing message. | SPF/DKIM checks not enforced strictly. | Configure email gateway to quarantine messages failing DMARC. | Email Admin | 2026-05-15 | In Progress |
| No alert on PowerShell download cradle. | PowerShell Script Block Logging not enabled on 20% of endpoints. | Deploy GPO to enable Script Block Logging globally. | Security Engineering | 2026-05-01 | Complete |
| Delayed communication with IT. | On-call contact list outdated. | Implement PagerDuty for automated on-call scheduling. | IT Ops Manager | 2026-06-01 | Not Started |

**Characteristics of Good Action Items:**
- **Specific:** 'Enable PowerShell logging' not 'Improve logging.'
- **Owned:** Assigned to a specific person or team.
- **Time-bound:** Clear due date.

**Follow-Up:** The Incident Commander should review this table **monthly** until all items are closed.

slides.title: The 'Draft' Watermark 🚧
slides.content:
# Controlling Distribution

**Never distribute the full Technical Report widely without controls.**

**Why?**
- **Discovery Risk:** The Technical Report contains a roadmap of your security failures. In a lawsuit, it's a goldmine for plaintiffs.
- **Insider Threat:** An employee with a grudge could leak the report to the press.

**Best Practices:**
- **Mark all drafts:** 'PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL - ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT - DRAFT' (if prepared at the direction of counsel).
- **Limit Distribution:** Executive Summary to Board. Technical Report to core security team and Legal.
- **Use Secure Sharing:** Password-protected PDFs, secure SharePoint links with expiration.
- **Final Version:** Store in a restricted, audited location. Do not email as an attachment.

quizData.question: The full Technical Incident Report should be emailed to all employees so everyone can learn from the incident.
quizData.explanation: False. Technical reports contain sensitive security details and potential admissions of liability. Distribution must be strictly limited.
